verdict.rationale: HelixDB documents official, published SDKs for Rust (helix-db 3.0.0 crate), TypeScript (@helix-db/helix-db 3.1.0), Go, and Python (helix-db 0.3.4 on PyPI). All four share one operation-tree request model, and the docs describe typed HTTP clients, an embedded client, and structured error metadata. Community comments criticize the query language but do not contradict that the SDKs exist or work. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of SDK usage, and a published version for the Go SDK.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: HelixDB v3 uses one operation-tree request model across the Rust, TypeScript, Go, and Python SDKs.
The published `helix-db` 3.0.0 crate provides the query DSL, request types, async HTTP client, native graph helpers, and a feature-gated embedded client.
The published `@helix-db/helix-db` 3.1.0 package targets Node.js 20 or newer and emits the same operation-tree AST as the Rust, Go, and Python SDKs.
The Go SDK builds the shared operation-tree AST and executes requests through a typed HTTP client.
The Python SDK is published on PyPI as `helix-db` 0.3.4 and imported as `helixdb`.
